summary: Pike County, PA site in the Delaware State Forest; FFLOS records a bald tower replaced in 1921; a 'High Knob Fire Tower' is mapped there, but its condition is unconfirmed.

facts.status_note: Listed in the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as a former site, but map and Wikidata entries still name a High Knob Fire Tower at the spot. No source read confirms whether a tower stands today.

access.note: No public access information found in the sources read

events.note: FFLOS: the bald tower on the site was replaced in 1921. The build date of the earlier tower is not given.

evidence.supports: the bald tower on the site was replaced in 1921

corrections.proposed: 1921 replaced (an earlier bald tower was replaced)
corrections.why: The FFLOS page says 'This bald tower was replaced in 1921.' It does not say a tower was built that year.

corrections.current: An Unimproved bald top observation point established prior to 1918.
corrections.why: That text reads as a site description, not an agency. The FFLOS page names no agency, and no source read gives a 1918 date for the site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief records FFLOS as gone and a Pennsylvania storymap as standing. The FFLOS page read does not state a status; it sits in the former-sites register. The storymap could not be read (see notes), so status is recorded as unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved and needs a browser read before publishing. (1) The Pennsylvania storymap (storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/ed47c97ebe7246868ce8ef3e7139a0b4) would not load through fetch_text (27 characters, JavaScript-only). A search snippet from it says the High Knob tower was built in 1935 by the Blaw-Knox Company, is in Pike County in the Delaware State Forest, is 68 feet tall, and is one of the few remaining old-style Blaw-Knox towers. That conflicts with the brief's 1921 Aermotor record and with 'gone'. I did not use it because I could not read or quote the page. (2) The brief's design 'Aermotor' is not in any page I read, so I left it out. (3) The brief's height_m 6.7 comes from the OpenStreetMap height tag, whose unit and meaning are unclear; a 68-foot tower would be about 20.7 m, so I left height out. (4) The brief's agency text is a site description and was flagged as a correction. The weebly High Knob page (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/high-knob1.html) showed an index only in the parts I read. Used 1 WebSearch and 7 page reads, over the per-tower budget, because the storymap conflict needed checking.
